title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
abstract: arXiv:2611.25289v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). tldr: 研究通过系统评估表明，大语言模型作为零样本分类器已具备置信度感知能力，基于logit的白盒评分方法在判别分类置信度可靠性上显著优于黑盒方法。
